# Manage multiple Claude Code sessions in parallel

> Follow requests for input in Paneflow, give each Claude Code session a clear task, and review changes in separate Git worktrees before merging.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/blog/run-multiple-claude-code-sessions

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

In Paneflow, you can run several Claude Code sessions side by side, each in its own terminal pane. Give each session a task that can move forward independently. When tasks need separate working files, use Git worktrees so you can review each contribution before merging it.

This guide covers Paneflow 0.17.5. You need Claude Code installed and authenticated in the shell you use. Paneflow is free and open source under GPL-3.0-or-later. Claude Code has its own access and usage conditions.

![Paneflow with an active Claude Code terminal and project tasks, branches, and activity states in the sidebar.](/images/task-context-window.webp)

## Independent sessions or subagents?

Use independent sessions when you want to direct each task yourself. Each has its own conversation; opening two panes does not automatically share their histories.

[Claude Code subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) handle delegated tasks in their own context and return results to a parent session. Choose them when you want one conversation to coordinate the work.

To combine different agents, see the [guide to running Claude Code and Codex together](/blog/run-claude-code-and-codex-in-parallel).

## Define a task for each session

Start with two tasks that do not depend on unfinished work. For example, one session can update `docs/setup.md` while another adds edge-case tests for an existing parser. If the tests need a parser rewrite that is still underway, finish that rewrite first.

Give each session:

- The expected result and the files it may edit.
- The existing behavior to preserve and the files assigned to another task.
- The checks to run and the decisions that need your input.

Keep project instructions in each checkout. Record any decisions the sessions need in a file they can read; a decision made in one conversation is not automatically available in another.

## Separate working files when needed

Two terminal panes can point to the same files. A Git worktree gives a task a separate working directory and branch.

For each task that needs this separation:

1. Add a pane in Paneflow and choose **New branch** in the branch selector.
2. Choose a branch name and the starting branch or commit. Keep **Worktree** enabled.
3. Open Claude Code in that worktree. Use the same starting commit for the other task if both should begin from the same code.

![Paneflow's New branch form with Worktree enabled and Claude Code among the launch choices.](/images/worktrees-new-branch.webp)

Before assigning work, check the directory, branch, and existing changes in each terminal:

```sh
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git branch --show-current
git status --short
```

For separate worktrees, the directories and branches should differ. Review any existing changes before letting a session edit files. The [Git worktree guide](/docs/worktrees) explains creation and reuse.

A read-only task can use a shared checkout, but it may see another session's edits while it reads. Sessions that edit shared files need explicit coordination. Worktrees also leave dependencies, server ports, and databases for you to manage separately.

## Follow requests for input

Check the Claude Code integration in [agent settings](/docs/settings). **Install hooks** enables activity reporting. The [agent supervision guide](/docs/features) explains the reported states and how tracking works without hooks.

When a session needs input, open its terminal and read the request before answering or approving it. When a turn finishes, review its output and changes. The activity indicator does not tell you whether the implementation is correct or the tests passed.

If an indicator seems wrong, read the terminal output before starting the same task again. Keep the number of sessions within what you can review and integrate.

## Review each result before merging

Save files you edited in Paneflow, then open **Changes** in the task's checkout. It compares staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files with that checkout's `HEAD`.

Check that the edits stay within the assigned task and run its required checks. Once you commit the changes, review the full branch diff separately: **Changes** shows local edits relative to `HEAD`.

Merge the reviewed contributions using your team's Git workflow. Resolve conflicts, read the combined diff, and run the project's checks on the merged result. Separate worktrees do not guarantee that the changes will work together.

## Return to a session later

To close Paneflow while leaving terminals active, choose **Keep sessions running**. Reopening the app reconnects to them while the session host and machine remain running. The [session persistence guide](/blog/keep-coding-agents-running) covers shutdown and sleep limits.

If a Claude Code process has ended, [the Sessions menu](/blog/agent-sessions) can load a saved conversation for the active directory. **Restart** starts a fresh shell; it does not resume that conversation.

### Can Paneflow manage multiple Claude Code sessions?

Yes. Paneflow runs independent Claude Code terminals and shows their project context and activity. You assign the tasks, answer requests, and review the results.

### Does each session need a Git worktree?

No. Use a worktree when a task needs separate working files and a branch. A read-only session can use a shared checkout if changes made by other sessions will not disrupt its investigation.

### Do more sessions avoid Claude Code usage limits?

No. Paneflow does not change the provider's account, concurrency, or usage limits. Reduce parallelism when sessions compete for the same quota or machine resources.
